findings.obligation: P12 (acceptance.md Covers row "keyboard user opens a row's actions menu and closes it with Escape", handoff F355): after Escape the table has neither scrolled nor changed its edge shadows. Falsifier F357: the grid jumps to its end when the button gets focus. Original Request: a keyboard user keeps their place in the table.
findings.observation: Commit 1ebc516de removed the two polls that falsified F355/F357 from thenActionsAreReachable: "closing the menu must not scroll the table; focusing the button moved it" (horizontalScrollPosition equal to the value before opening) and "closing the menu must leave the shadows as they were" (sidesWithACue equal to before). The declared expectation text is still in acceptance.md and handoff.json; the Disposition now says "a check that fails to notice this jump still passes". The jump is an observed production behaviour: crafter run craft.S3.json (second pass) records the scroller jumping to 340 when the menu opens at 375 px, and the browser check failing at 0 expected / 340 received before the scroll-guard change. The known limitation was decided by the root (1ebc516de message, root context), not by the maintainer; no human scope amendment with provenance exists in feature-delta.md decision table (decision 7 covers only the menu). So the oracle now accepts a declared falsifier as passing. Static review only, Playwright not run per instruction.
findings.remediation: Restore both polls in thenActionsAreReachable: horizontalScrollPosition after Escape equals the value taken before the menu opened, and sidesWithACue after Escape equals the value taken before. Keep them RED against current production until the jump is fixed (implementation finding, slice review). Do not approve a state where a declared falsifier passes. If the maintainer, not the root, decides to defer the jump, the deferral goes into acceptance.md and feature-delta.md with the maintainer as provenance and the check states that deferral explicitly; the host decides the escalation.

findings.obligation: P12 / F357 falsifier: the Name clear of the pinned column must be an observation, not a state change; a grid jump to its end must be observable
findings.observation: OverviewPage.ts nameCanBeReadClearOfActions (lines 242-257): clear() is evaluated first; if the Name does not lie clear of the pinned actions column, the helper calls scrollToTheStart() (line 255, sets scrollLeft = 0 and dispatches a scroll event) and evaluates clear() again. Consequence: (a) if the grid has jumped to its end, the Name is scrolled off to the left, so clear() is already true and the poll passes on the jump state itself; (b) otherwise the helper resets the scroll position before the second read. Either way the poll cannot observe the jump that F357 names, and the spec's poll at OverviewTableFit.spec.ts:45 reads the result as "Name readable". A check that mutates the state it reads is not a pure observation. Non-vacuous only for a Name that stays under the pinned column at scroll start. Static analysis; not executed.
findings.remediation: Make nameCanBeReadClearOfActions a read-only observation: read the Name box and the actions header box in the current state, and separately read horizontalScrollPosition; drop the scrollToTheStart() call from inside the poll. The Name check then fails on a jump, and the scroll check (restored per the first finding) fails on the same state. A scroll-back, if needed, belongs in the spec body after the observation, not inside the predicate.

findings.obligation: P12 keyboard exposure of the actions menu (L4); non-blocking
findings.observation: The focus-return test (DataOverviewTable.test.tsx:1131-1148) focuses the button, presses Enter, awaits the menu, presses Escape and asserts the button has focus. It never asserts that focus entered the menu while it was open, so an implementation that never moves focus into the menu passes the test. Same gap was raised as non-blocking F1 in the earlier slice review (runs/review.oracle.S3.json) and is still present. Non-blocking.
findings.remediation: Before pressing Escape, assert the menu item (or the menu list) holds focus, then assert the button holds focus after Escape. Non-blocking; owner oracle; affected phase: S3 completion.
